text:
alex: Heads-up — we keep seeing billing attribution + quota spikes in dashboards when SA requests hit fallback routing. Can we sync on what telemetry is missing?

sam: I noticed that too. example: requests from org X route to project fallback P and quota shows against P but console shows original SA. confusing for customers.

maria: Are we sure the router is returning the final effective identity in headers? I think the gateway only sets `X-Effective-Project` for internal metrics, not logs.

kevin: That's the crux. router decision is emitted to our ring buffer but not to the user-facing telemetry pipeline. we need an event at decision time: `auth.routing.decision` with fields for `requested_identity`, `effective_identity`, `route_reason`, `quota_project`, `model_variant`.

jess: Agree on the event. UX asks for a simple tile: "Effective billing project" next to token usage so CS can triage quickly. rollout behind flag.

maria: Proposed event payload (rough):
```
{
  "requested_identity": "sa:team-llm@org",
  "effective_identity": "project:fallback-p",
  "route_reason": "capacity_fallback",
  "quota_project": "proj-fallback-p",
  "decision_ts": "...",
  "sampled": false
}
```

sam: quick thought — adding all these events will explode cardinality. we should sample by org and only include full payload on sampled traces. non-sampled should emit a compact metric e.g. `auth.routing.count` with tags `reason`, `is_fallback`.

kevin: yep — metric + sampled event pattern. also include a `routing_hash` so we can correlate metric -> event in logs when we need to. keep string fields short (ids, not full emails).

jess: For console rollouts: feature flag `auth.routing.telemetry.v2`. start with 10% internal orgs, 100% for SRE + support. Add a dashboard tile and a quick drill: click the tile -> logs view filtered to `routing_hash`.

alex: Ops question: does Dedicated/Dedicated-Private use same headers? we can't leak tenant ids across private control planes.

maria: Private deployments will emit events to customer KMS / local telemetry only. our public metrics will get aggregated counts only. need a config knob `emit_full_routing_event` default false for private.

ops-bot: @channel deploy queued for router changes in canary ring (canary-3). CI green.

kevin: Implementation checklist:
- router: attach minimal `effective_identity` + `routing_hash` to request context (low overhead).
- metrics: increment `auth.routing.count{reason,is_fallback}` (high-cardinality safe).
- telemetry pipeline: sampled sink for full events, TTL-limited storage (30 days).
- console: new card + drilldown to logs by `routing_hash`.

sam: UX detail — product asks that the console label the "billed project" and separately show the "acting service account" so customers don't confuse ownership. also show last 24h count of fallback decisions.

jess: We'll mock the tile in figma and link to the telemetry schema. canary rollout plan in PR.

alex: One more: fallback decisions should trigger a light alert when a single org hits >1% fallback rate for 1h. ops want heads-up before CS tickets.

kevin: Agreed. Add rule to alerts: `sum(auth.routing.count{is_fallback,org=~"$ORG"}[1h]) / sum(auth.total.requests{org=~"$ORG"}[1h]) > 0.01` -> paged to oncall. sampling shouldn't affect the metric counts.

maria: I'll open a PR with the schema and conservative sampling config. tagging @kevin @jess for review.

alex: Thanks. if folks can review quickly we can land the router change tomorrow in canary. :thumbsup: 

infra-bot: deploy started for canary-3 at `2026-03-23T17:22:00Z`. monitor /deployments/canary-3 for logs.

sam: will follow metrics and post a short runbook snippet in #eng-oncall for how to interpret the new tile.

jess: added mock to internal figma board: https://figma.com/file/xxx/auth-routing-tile -> comments welcome. :sparkles: 

alex: Great work. follow-ups: PR links, alert rule, and console mock. I'll put those in a single tracker and ping the channel when ready.
